Our story

Karl & Blessing, so far

Real photos from Karl's trip to Nigeria in October and November 2026.

Chapter 1 · Feb 28, 2025 → October 2026

From a screen to the same room

Karl and Blessing have been together since February 28, 2025, with Karl in Chicago and Blessing in Nigeria. For twenty months, their relationship lived in messages and video calls across an ocean.

In October 2026 Karl flew to Lagos. At the airport, through a crowd of people, there she was: standing out, more beautiful than he remembered. For the first time they were in the same room.

Chapter 2 · November 2, 2026

The question

First, Karl went to her family's home, met her parents, her sisters and her brother, and was welcomed.

Only after meeting her family did he give her the ring. On November 2, 2026, in Lagos, Karl asked Blessing to marry him. She said yes.

After twenty months apart and a few days side by side, it wasn't a hard question. Karl puts it simply: they are one.

The ring was on her hand, and the plan was to spend Christmas together in Chicago.

Two years earlier, the K-1 fiancé visa route had been blocked for them, so they chose a B-2 visitor visa, just to get Blessing to America. Karl made sure to visit her in person before her interview, and he did.

Her interview was set for November 10, 2026. She was dressed and ready, and Karl had booked her a hotel near the embassy, because it is too far from her home to make it there on time. That is when they first heard about the ban.

They had been so focused on the excitement of seeing each other and finally being together that the terrible news slipped right past them.

Presidential Proclamation 10998 had quietly taken effect on January 1, 2026. Nigeria is one of 19 countries under a partial U.S. visa suspension: no new B-1/B-2 visitor visas, no new student or exchange visas, and immigrant visas suspended except in narrow cases. Nigerians can still apply and sit for the interview, but the visa can't be issued.

Three weeks later, on January 21, 2026, the U.S. paused immigrant visa processing for Nigeria and about 74 other countries.

Chapter 3 · The wall

Then came the goodbye

Karl was already back in Chicago when the news hit, and Blessing was in Lagos. Disappointed, he told her not to spend the day traveling to the embassy for a visa the ban wouldn't let them issue.

Under the ban, Blessing can't visit Chicago, not even for Christmas.

They aren't waiting on the ban to be together again. That's where Morocco comes in.

Why Morocco

Neutral ground — a fresh start, together

Morocco belongs to neither of them — and that is exactly the point. It is not Karl's Chicago and it is not Blessing's Nigeria. It is a neutral place in between, where they can meet as equals, leave what happened before behind them, and start this chapter clean. Karl is a lifelong Chicagoan — author, musician, and photographer from Pullman, and founder of Melori. Blessing is in Nigeria. He proposed in Lagos on November 2, 2026 and she said yes.

The short version

Morocco is neutral ground. It isn't Karl's home turf and it isn't Blessing's — it is a place that belongs to neither of them, so it can belong to both of them. What happened in Nigeria stays in Nigeria; Morocco is clear of it — a clean, fresh place to be together without anything from before hanging over these three weeks.

The practical reason they need neutral ground is brief: under Proclamation 10998, Nigerian immigrant and visitor visas are suspended, so Blessing cannot come to the U.S. right now and the couple's K-1 fiancé visa path is blocked while the ban stands. Karl has taken their case to Congress with his Citizen Accountability Clause proposal, and that fight continues. Morocco, by contrast, welcomes both of them — Blessing on an e-visa, Karl from Chicago — for 22 days they get what most couples take for granted: Christmas morning together, New Year together, and time to plan a wedding and a future.

It won't be only a holiday. Karl will be photographing, filming, and writing songs in Marrakech — and sharing all of it as it happens. Supporters aren't funding a vacation postcard; they're standing behind a couple, and coming along for the whole journey.

Shared with care: Karl is keeping this ask inside the communities who already know their story — especially the K-1 groups walking the same road — rather than broadcasting it across his photography business. If you're here, you're one of those people. Thank you.

Honest answers

Questions people ask

How do I donate, and how do I get RELAUNCH, Karl Ray's R&B album?

Tap one of the four amounts in Support the trip. Each one opens Stripe's secure checkout. Give $20 or more and your RELAUNCH download link appears on the confirmation screen right after you pay. Save that link.

Do I have to donate to follow the trip?

No. Following is free for everyone. Create a free account at melorimusic.org/register and you'll see the photos, updates, and first listens Karl posts from Morocco. Support and the album are a separate, optional exchange.

Why is the goal only $977 when the trip costs about $3,568?

Because Karl is earning his share. His photography and portrait work cover his flight, the apartment, and food. The $977 community goal is only Blessing's flight ($837) and e-visa ($140) — the pieces that have to be booked first before fares rise.

Why Morocco? Why can't Blessing just visit Chicago?

Because Morocco is neutral ground — not Karl's home and not Blessing's home, a fresh place that belongs to neither of them and is clear of what came before. What happened in Nigeria stays in Nigeria; Morocco starts clean. Practically, it also works: under the current proclamation, Nigerian visitor and immigrant visas are suspended, so a U.S. visit isn't available to Blessing right now — and the couple's earlier K-1 attempt never reached an interview for the same reason. Morocco admits both of them, so it's where they can meet on equal ground. Karl's advocacy for a fix — his Citizen Accountability Clause — continues in parallel.

When do postcards and prints arrive?

Postcards are written and mailed from Marrakech during the trip (international post takes its own sweet time). Signed prints are photographed in Morocco, then printed and signed by Karl after he returns to Chicago on Jan 6. Signed copies of Without The Blacks: The Complete Edition for Collector-tier supporters are likewise signed and shipped in January, after the trip. And if your support was $20 or more, RELAUNCH is delivered to you automatically as a digital album as soon as your support lands.

What if the trip falls short?

The plan has a guardrail Karl set himself: no new debt for this trip. The booking order protects supporters too — Blessing's e-visa and flight come first, and the apartment is on free cancellation. If the money isn't there by Dec 5, the dates shorten or shift rather than a card getting swiped.
